subject: gk
question: The Stupa sculptures found at Sanghol in Punjab belongs to which of the following schools?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mathura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Stupa sculptures found at Sanghol in Punjab belong to the **Mathura school of art**.
 
• The Mathura school of art is known for its distinctive style characterized by the depiction of Buddha in human form and elaborate decorative elements.
 
• The sculptures from Mathura exhibit a strong sense of movement and vitality, often showcasing intricate carvings and detailed drapery.
 
• The Mathura school flourished during the Kushan period, particularly under the patronage of rulers like Kanishka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhara School of Art**:

 
 
• The Gandhara school emerged in the region of modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan during the Kushan period.
 
• It is renowned for its Greco-Roman influence, evident in the realistic representation of human figures and drapery.
 
• This school primarily used grey schist stone for its sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Sarnath School of Art**:
 
 
• Sarnath, near Varanasi, became an important center for Buddhist art during the Gupta period.
 
• The sculptures from Sarnath are noted for their serene and compassionate expressions, depicting Buddha in a more spiritual and ethereal manner.
 
• Polished sandstone was commonly used in the Sarnath school.
 
 
 
• **Amravati School of Art**:
 
 
• The Amravati school flourished in the Andhra region, particularly around the Krishna River, during the Satavahana period.
 
• It is known for its dynamic and detailed narrative panels depicting scenes from the life of Buddha.
 
• White marble was often used for the sculptures from this school.
